    34	/--
    35	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    36	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    37	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    38	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    39	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    40	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    41	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`,
    42	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    43	-/
    44	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    45	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    46	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    47	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    48	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    49	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    50	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    51	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    52	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    53	
    54	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    55	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    56	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    58	-/
    59	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    60	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    63	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    64	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    66	-/
    67	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    68	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    69	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    70	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    71	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    72	      fun x =>
    73	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    74	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    75	
    76	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    77	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    80	-/
    81	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    82	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    83	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    84	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    85	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    86	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    87	
    88	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    89	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    90	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`, paper origin
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    92	-/
    93	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    94	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    95	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    96	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    97	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    98	
    99	/--
   100	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
   101	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1185-1195`; paper
   102	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
   103	-/
   104	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   105	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   106	
   107	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   108	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation
   109	construction of `lem:cl-concat`. -/
   110	private def CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   111	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : (ell : ℕ) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   112	  | 0 => .zero
   113	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)
   114	
   115	@[simp]
   116	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   117	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (x : ι → K) :
   118	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   119	  induction ell with
   120	  | zero => rfl
   121	  | succ ell ih =>
   122	      simp [CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval, ih]
   123	
   124	private theorem CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   125	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) :
   280	  induction t generalizing acc SU with
   281	  | zero =>
   282	      exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono
   283	        (CondLinearTerm.liftRight_supportedOn (hr acc)) Finset.subset_union_right
   284	  | @succ k S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   285	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   286	      refine ⟨(Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hS₁).trans Finset.subset_union_left,
   287	        fun y => ?_⟩
   288	      have hrec := ih (fun i => y (.inl i)) (acc := acc + fun i => y (.inl i))
   289	        (hrest (fun i => y (.inl i)))
   290	      have hsets :
   291	          (SU \ S₁).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪ SV.map Function.Embedding.inr =
   292	            (SU.map Function.Embedding.inl ∪ SV.map Function.Embedding.inr) \
   293	              S₁.map Function.Embedding.inl := by
   294	        ext i
   295	        cases i <;> simp
   296	      simpa only [hsets] using hrec
   297	
   298	/--
   299	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   300	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   301	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1199-1202`, paper origin
   302	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   303	-/
   304	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   305	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   306	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   307	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   308	
   309	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   310	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   311	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   312	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   313	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1235-1249`, paper origin
   314	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   315	-/
   316	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   317	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   318	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   319	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   320	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   321	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   322	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   323	
   324	/--
   325	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   326	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1235-1249`, with
   327	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-292`.
   328	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   329	-/
   330	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   331	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   332	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   333	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   334	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   335	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   336	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   337	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   338	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   339	  classical
   340	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   341	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   342	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   343	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   344	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   345	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   346	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   347	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   348	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   349	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   350	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   351	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   352	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   353	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   354	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   355	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   356	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   357	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   358	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   359	    have huniv :
   360	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   361	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   362	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   363	      ext i
   364	      cases i <;> simp
   365	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   366	  · funext x
   367	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   368	    simp only [zero_add]
   369	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   370	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   371	    rfl

   373	/--
   374	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   375	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   376	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1365-1377`;
   377	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   378	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   379	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   380	-/
   381	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   382	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   383	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   384	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   385	
   386	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   387	nonempty.  This is not a named statement of the source article; it is
   388	`lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   389	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1379-1389`. -/
   390	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   391	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   392	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   393	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   394	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   395	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   396	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   397	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   398

   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0

   205	    | .inr _ => 0

   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every

   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>

   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0

   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl

   231	    · simp

   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl

   238	      rfl

     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-520`;
    14	the formalization support nodes `lem:line-rep-kernel` and
    15	`lem:line-rep-incidence` are at `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:522-550`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators
    22	
    23	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    24	
    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    30	-/
    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34	
    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    38	-/
    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    45	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 464-478; paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    47	-/
    48	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    49	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    50	
    51	/--
    52	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    53	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`; paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    55	-/
    56	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    57	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    58	
    59	/--
    60	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    61	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:480-486`,
    62	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    63	-/
    64	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    65	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    66	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    67	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := h
    68	  ext x
    69	  constructor
    70	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    71	    exact ⟨s - t, by module⟩
    72	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    73	    exact ⟨t + s, by module⟩
    74	
    75	/--
    76	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    77	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    78	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    79	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:500-520`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    81	-/
    82	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    83	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=

    86	\begin{definition}[Canonical complement]\label{def:canonical-complement}
    87		\uses{def:register-subspace}
    88		Let $\hat{E}$ be the standard basis of $V = \F^n$ and let
    89		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subset V$ be a set of $m$ linearly independent
    90		vectors. Write $v_i = \sum_{j=1}^n a_{i,j}\, \hat{e}_j$, and, using a
    91		canonical Gaussian-elimination algorithm valid over arbitrary fields,
    92		transform the $m \times n$ matrix $(a_{i,j})$ to reduced row echelon form
    93		$(b_{i,j})$. Let $J$ be the set of $m$ column indices containing the leading
    94		$1$ entry of each row of $(b_{i,j})$. The \emph{canonical complement of $F$}
    95		is the set of $n - m$ standard basis vectors
    96		\[
    97			F^\perp = \{\hat{e}_j : j \notin J\}\;.
    98		\]
    99		The canonical complement is a \emph{set} of vectors, not a subspace.

   114	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:canonical-complement}
   115		\uses{def:canonical-complement, def:complementary}
   116		Let $S$ be the span of linearly independent vectors
   117		$F = \{v_1, \dots, v_m\} \subseteq V$, let $F^\perp$ be the canonical
   118		complement of $F$, and let $T = \mathrm{span}(F^\perp)$. Then
   119		\[
   120			S + T = V\;, \qquad S \cap T = \{0\}\;.

   123	\begin{proof}
   124		\uses{def:canonical-complement}
   125		Let $A = (a_{i,j})$ be the $m \times n$ matrix whose rows are the $v_i$ and
   126		write $A = UB$ with $U$ invertible and $B$ in reduced row echelon form, so

   128		of the rows of $B$ to the columns in $J$ are still linearly independent and

   131		coordinates outside $J$, that is, $u - v \in T$, which proves $S + T = V$.

item.text: The audit is complete. The line geometry and marginal statements themselves align, but the typed-conditionally-linear claims still overstate what the linked Lean declarations establish, and several dependency/status records remain inaccurate.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:87` — The `\leanok` claims a typed-conditionally-linear family result, while the linked theorem proves only equality to an unconstrained distribution constructor.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:395` — The Pauli source node links an equality-only open theorem rather than the stated typed-conditionally-linear assertion.
- [ ] F3 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1359` — The blueprint quantifies over a finite type set, but the linked Lean definition permits an arbitrary type.
- [ ] F4 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistributionAux.lean:203` — Eight new public distribution lemmas lack blueprint support nodes and dependency records.
- [ ] F5 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:69` — The affine- and diagonal-line level proofs cite `lem:cl-concat`, which neither linked Lean proof invokes.
- [ ] F6 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:109` — The ALNF and DLNF proof dependencies omit the distribution, representative, and diagonal-prefix results used by the Lean proofs.
- [ ] F7 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinear.lean:9` — The module descriptions use implementation-history language instead of describing the mathematical relationship between the results.
- [ ] F8 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinearTheorems.lean:27` — “Stage” remains as process-oriented terminology where the mathematics uses levels and linear contributions.
